title: Dynamic per-customer cost policy enforcer for batching & KV-cache tuning
creator: Ava Ramirez
description: Build an automated enforcer and UI integration that recommends and safely applies per-customer and per-route batching + KV-cache configurations. The goal is to reduce per-token cost while keeping latency and correctness within SLOs. The system will produce segmentation-based policies (by customer tier, traffic shape, and route semantics), allowlists/denylists for caching and aggressive batching, and tiered controls so enterprise customers can lock settings. Must include safe apply and automated rollback hooks tied to observable thresholds.
updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff meeting - aligned on three workstreams: recommendation engine, safe-apply runtime hook, and Console UX for policy review.

2026-02-25: Prototype of recommendation engine completed using 30 days of token-level telemetry. Initial heuristics: classify traffic by median seq length, prefix reuse rate, and 95th percentile latency sensitivity.

2026-03-03: Design review notes incorporated - Product asked for explicit denylist support for sensitive routes (e.g., PII-heavy endpoints). Design suggested a per-route 'no-cache' override and per-customer 'allow-aggressive-batching' flag.

2026-03-06: Implemented server-side safe-apply: feature-flagged endpoint PATCH /internal/policies/apply that can run in dry-run, canary (pct rollout), and full modes. Added audit log entries to internal-audit cluster.

2026-03-09: Canary deploy 5% traffic for 'tier:gold' customers. Observed ~18% token-cost reduction and +12ms median latency on test routes. Error rate unchanged. Added automated rollback rule to revert when p95 latency increases >30% or error rate >2x baseline.
2026-03-11: Security review flagged need to exclude on-prem Private customers by default. Updated policy schema to include deployment_scope and enforcement_mode attributes.
2026-03-12: Engineering spike to persist per-customer policy history for audit and rollback; added PR reference (see links).
acceptance_criteria: Recommendations: system surfaces per-customer + per-route recommendations with estimated cost delta and risk score in Console
Safe apply: operator can apply in dry-run/canary/full modes; canary percentage adjustable; automated rollback triggers based on configurable thresholds
Policies: support segmentation keys (customer_tier, route_pattern, region), allowlist/denylist semantics for caching and batching, and 'locked_by_customer' flag
Telemetry: new dashboard showing cost delta, latency p50/p95, error rate, and cache-hit ratio for affected routes within 15m resolution
Auditability: every policy apply/rollback stored with user, timestamp, diff, and linked PR/Runbook
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal dry-run + manual review (2 weeks). Phase 2: 5% canary on non-enterprise customers with automated rollback hooks (1 week). Phase 3: tiered rollout with controls for enterprise customers and Console approval flow (2-3 weeks).
implementation_notes: Recommendation engine runs nightly using a job that clusters routes by seq_len distribution and cache_prefix_reuse. Rules are generated as JSON policy blobs and scored. Runtime accepts policy blob and reconciles via policy-enforcer service; enforcer communicates with serving-runtime to adjust batch_size, kv_cache_enabled, and cache_ttl. We add a safety layer: any change must pass a simulated dry-run cost/latency estimator before canary. Use feature flag 'cost-policy-enforcer-v1' to gate rollout.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Aggressive batching reduces cost but increases tail latency for latency-sensitive routes. KV cache can return stale or incorrect tokens for dynamic content; denylist required. Rolling out changes automatically may surprise customers; therefore provide opt-out and 'locked_by_customer' semantics. Canarying on low-volume routes may underrepresent impact on high-volume traffic patterns.
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus on the automated rollback thresholds and whether the denylist semantics are sufficiently expressive to capture compliance constraints. Check PR #2345 for runtime hooks and PR #2359 for Console UI. Ops should validate log volume impact for audit trails.
qa_steps: 1) Run recommendation job in dry-run against prod-like dataset and confirm recommendations for three test customers
2) Apply policy in canary mode to test cohort and exercise traffic generator, verify no >30% p95 latency increase
3) Trigger simulated rollback by artificially increasing latency and confirm policy-enforcer reverts settings and records audit entry
4) Validate Console shows policy diff, risk score, and 'apply' controls for admins
